Those rupee figures are APMC Karjat's prices, not Nashik's — APMC Karjat is the median mandi for onion statewide and is what this sell-vs-store call is priced from. Check the price-and-selling card for what Nashik itself reported.
Hold-vs-sell needs warehouse cost, spoilage, and price-recovery data; none are in the real sources, so the engine recommends selling now (or abstains) — it never fabricates a store case.

Scope: this sell-now-vs-store call is CROP-LEVEL. It is priced off a representative (median) mandi for onion across the state — APMC Karjat (Ahilyanagar district) — which is a REFERENCE price, not a recommendation to travel there. You asked about Nashik, so storage availability below is for Nashik district.

WDRA-registered warehouses in Nashik: 15 active of 21 registered (~106,325 MT active capacity). Real operating storage EXISTS in your district (WDRA public directory); this is district availability, not a per-farmer booking or the storage cost.

Warehouse infrastructure in Nashik (AIF projects, UNCALIBRATED context): 10 storage project(s) — 10 cold-storage. Storage infrastructure EXISTS in your district; the next step to evaluate holding is a warehouse/FPO quote for storage cost + spoilage (still not in open data).

Storage-cost reference: CWC publishes warehouse storage tariffs (cewacor.nic.in, 30% farmer rebate); this crop is not in the committed commodity tariff, so enter your warehouse's actual Rs/quintal/month to hold.

What this crop has sold for (real, committed Agmarknet percentiles over 963 trading days, 2024-01-01 to 2026-08-26, about 2.7 years): about Rs 1150.0/1400.0/2150.0 per quintal (low/typical/high across those days). That is how the statewide daily median price moved from day to day over that whole period — a record of PAST prices, not today's price and not a forecast. Today's price is stated separately on this card.

Storage history (25 years of government mandi prices, Agmarknet): holding Onion from September for 2 months — past years DISAGREED: a typical year gained 33.0%, but in 1 year out of 4 it lost 3.3% or more, and in 1 year out of 4 it gained 56.3% or more. The bad years were mild next to the good ones (3.3% against 56.3%), but the record cannot tell you which kind of year this is. The record does not settle whether to store. And holding from September for 4 months (typically about 10.5% down) also LOST value in a typical year — not in every year, because the best quarter of years still gained, but more often than not. This is what past years did — it is not a forecast of this year.

No loan context provided — assuming no urgent repayment deadline.

PRICE IS NOT NASHIK'S: the rupee figures on this card are APMC Karjat (Ahilyanagar district) — the median mandi for onion statewide — because that is the representative price this sell-vs-store call is built on. They are NOT Nashik prices. Check the price-and-selling card for what your own district reported.

No warehouse/e-NWR economics (storage cost per quintal-month, spoilage rate, loan-to-value, interest) are available in the real sources, so the engine cannot recommend HOLDING — it sells now or abstains rather than invent a store case. To evaluate holding, consult a registered warehouse / FPO for these figures.

YOU WERE NOT ASKED WHETHER YOU CAN STORE. This answer assumes you cannot, and that assumption is the whole reason it says sell now — while our own records show active registered warehouses in Nashik. If you can reach a warehouse, cold store, an FPO's storage or your own safe dry space, this is the wrong answer for you: ask again with that in mind, and get a storage quote first.
Whether storing Onion from September pays is NOT settled by the record: past years split between gains and losses over the same period.
Holding Onion from September came out worse, not better, over 4 months. A shorter hold looking good does not make a longer one safe.

A TYPICAL YEAR IS NOT THE ONLY YEAR. Holding Onion from September for 3 months (about +10.8% in a typical year, but -26.8% or worse in one year out of four). The typical figure does not tell you that, and the money at risk in a bad year is a quarter of the outcomes, not a rare accident. Decide on what you could afford to lose, not on the middle.

The storage-history figures for Onion are the change in MANDI PRICE only. Storage charges, weight loss, quality loss and the cost of waiting for the money are NOT deducted — your actual return is lower, and a small gain can still be a loss.

Onion is stored in practice, but it loses weight and quality while stored far faster than grain does. Treat the price history above as the ceiling, not the outcome, and ask locally what shrinkage to expect before deciding.

IF YOU CAN STORE, THIS IS NOT YOUR ANSWER. Holding 2 months from this month changed the price by about +33.0% in a typical year, and Nashik has active registered warehouses. That figure is the change in MANDI PRICE and this crop also loses weight and quality while stored, which it does not deduct. Get a storage-cost quote before deciding; the recommendation above assumes you have no storage because you were not asked.
